transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-03
Time: 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Omar Singh, Lena Park (Redwood) — Raj Patel, Sofia Martinez, Daniel Cho, Priya Nair, Alex Kim (Vanguard HealthTech)

Summary:
Brief: Weekly POC check-in focused on final go/no-go decision criteria, fallback/runbook alignment, canary sizing and monitoring thresholds. Action items assigned for runbook, warmup tooling, and security confirmations.
Topics: runbook review; canary target & telemetry; thresholds and SLO gating; rollback vs abort decision tree; KMS & audit log handoff; cost/latency tradeoffs; A/B experiment gating

Action items (quick list): Maya to send runbook, Omar to send warmup script, Raj to schedule canary, Priya to confirm security artifacts.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay, thanks everyone for joining. Agenda is pretty focused — finalize the go decision and make sure the fallback playbook is tidy. We have 60 minutes, so let's hit the main bullets.
[00:18] Raj Patel: Yep thanks. We had one internal dry run yesterday, some warm cache issues — the first 30 to 60 seconds spike in latency. Wanted to surface that up front.
[00:29] Omar Singh: That sounds like cold KV cache miss pattern. In Redwood's testing we saw the initial prefix/KV cash fill causes token latency spikes until warm up completes. I sent a sketch of a warmup script earlier, happy to walk through it.
[00:45] Sofia Martinez: Can you repeat KV cash — is that the key value? The transcript sometimes reads cache as cash, hah.
[00:50] Omar Singh: Sorry yes cache. The warmup reduces cold-start tokens and evictions.
[00:58] Daniel Cho: From our side we want a deterministic canary plan. We're leaning to a small A/B first, 10% traffic for 6 hours, then expand to 30% if signals look good. What telemetry should gate expansion?
[01:12] Lena Park: Great question. We recommend a three-tier gate: latency p50/p95 not exceeding target; error-rate per-route below X% (we defined X in the runbook draft); and model quality checks — a small prompt set evaluation for regression.
[01:25] Maya Chen: I'll call out concrete numbers: p95 < 650ms for the inference path (customer target is 700), error rate < 0.5% for 5xx and 4xx; and a quality regression threshold of >2% drop on the PR curve for our evaluation prompts should block expansion.
[01:40] Raj Patel: That p95 number seems aggressive with our current infra. We're seat-of-pants; under load we saw p95 at ~820ms when the pool scaled. We need to balance cost and latency.
[01:52] Omar Singh: Two levers — warmup + pre-warming reserved capacity. For POC we can use a dedicated burst for the canary window or run with hosted instances but with more aggressive batching. Batching trades latency for tokens/cost.
[02:08] Sofia Martinez: If we pre-warm, what's the burn cost? We need a sense of delta for finance signoff.
[02:16] Maya Chen: We'll attach a cost delta table with options: no pre-warm, minimal pre-warm, full reserved burst. Rough numbers: minimal pre-warm increases cost by ~12% in the window, full reserved burst ~35% but p95 drops substantially. I'll include those numbers.
[02:31] Alex Kim: For rollback vs abort — can you explain the difference operationally? We've conflated them in our runbooks.
[02:37] Omar Singh: Good distinction. Abort = stop the rollout attempt and route back to previous stable configuration immediately; rollback = actively revert stateful changes, e.g., model version pinned to previous with a DB migration undo — more stateful. For our inference-only change, it's usually abort traffic shift.
[02:58] Daniel Cho: So abort is safer. What about half-rollbacks or gradual rollbacks?
[03:03] Lena Park: We have an automated traffic gating step: if any of the gating metrics breach threshold by more than 1.5x for 2 consecutive evaluation windows, we abort and shift 100% back. We can make that a gradual backoff but that adds complexity and risk for user-visible regressions.
[03:20] Priya Nair: Security question — KMS rotation and audit trail needs to be in the runbook. We can't have manual key rotates without documented steps. Also need to confirm where logs are stored and retention for compliance.
[03:30] Maya Chen: Agreed. Priya, we're planning to include KMS integration notes and sample key rotation commands. We also will point to audit logs export path in the console. 
[03:40] Priya Nair: Can you include SAML SSO flows? Our IdP team wants to ensure tokens are not persisted incorrectly.
[03:45] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include SSO notes and the RBAC step — who has rollback permission.
[03:50] Raj Patel: On monitoring — what's the minimum dashboard we need for the canary? CPU/GPU utilization, throughput, p50/p95, token cost per request, error rates, and the prompt-set eval pass rate, correct?
[04:02] Omar Singh: Exactly. Also include model-level health like kv-cache hit rate, batch sizes in flight, and queue depth. The Redwood console exposes these; we'll share dashboard links.
[04:15] Daniel Cho: For A/B: we want to measure quality delta vs latency. How do you recommend instrumenting that? We can tag responses and do offline scoring?
[04:23] Lena Park: Two approaches: (1) inline scoring for a small sampled set and (2) offline evaluation with a golden set. Inline gives fast feedback but adds overhead. For the POC, sample 2% of requests for inline scoring and compare to a history baseline.
[04:38] Alex Kim: We also want rollout windows — should we do the canary during off-peak or do a constant small percent?
[04:45] Maya Chen: Recommend an off-peak canary for first try, then a small continuous ramp for the following day. Off-peak reduces blast radius and gives clearer signals.
[04:55] Sofia Martinez: Scheduling question — do you need a dedicated maintenance window? Our ops prefer weekends.
[04:58] Raj Patel: Weekend works; we'll propose Saturday 01:00 – 07:00 local.
[05:03] Omar Singh: On the technical side, also ensure the KV cache warmup is run across all inference nodes in the pool. The warmup script will pad in initial tokens to populate key shards. It should be idempotent.
[05:16] Daniel Cho: Will pre-warm cause model quality issues due to different tokenization?
[05:20] Omar Singh: No, warmup is just inference requests against known prompts to populate KV. It shouldn't change model weights.
[05:26] Priya Nair: Where do we keep the test prompts? We need them in the repo with limited access.
[05:30] Maya Chen: We'll share a secured Google Drive link and also a copy in the project's S3 with restricted IAM.
[05:36] Alex Kim: On metrics gating, how long is the evaluation window? 5 min? 15 min?
[05:40] Lena Park: For canary we recommend 5-minute evaluation windows, but require two consecutive windows to fail before abort. So effectively 10 minutes of sustained failure.
[05:50] Raj Patel: That seems reasonable — but our alerting latency is sometimes delayed by metric collection. We may need to tune scrape intervals.
[05:56] Omar Singh: We'll provide recommended scrape intervals and the Redwood tracing hooks to reduce metric lag.
[06:03] Maya Chen: Okay, let's run through the runbook steps quickly: <read brief outline of steps> 1) pre-checks (SLO baseline, backups, KMS) 2) pre-warm 3) start 10% canary 4) monitor two windows 5) expand or abort 6) post-check and rollback if needed.
[06:22] [laughter] Sofia Martinez: Classic. Who owns step 3?
[06:25] Raj Patel: Ops will own start, but Redwood will provide the scripted commands so it's reproducible.
[06:30] Maya Chen: Omar will hand over the script and Lena will own the gating thresholds in the console.
[06:35] Omar Singh: I'll also attach a small health-check endpoint that returns current KV hit rate and estimated warmness. It's a small shim.
[06:45] Daniel Cho: For canary scaling, what about autoscaler behavior? We saw some oscillations.
[06:50] Omar Singh: Tune the autoscaler with hysteresis and set min-capacity during canary window. For the POC, set min nodes to 60% of expected peak to avoid thrash.
[06:59] Maya Chen: Financial ask — Alex, any blockers for paying for pre-warm?
[07:03] Alex Kim: Need finance approvals but if you can provide clear delta and a rollback guarantee, we'll likely greenlight minimal pre-warm.
[07:10] Maya Chen: We'll include a conditional clause in runbook: if pre-warm approved, set policy A; else policy B (longer warmup + slower ramp).
[07:20] Priya Nair: One more security item: we require proof of data handling for the sampled inline scoring. Are the sampled responses redacted?
[07:28] Omar Singh: Yes, Redwood can apply redact rules — we'll document the PII strip pipeline and ensure sampled traces are only viewable by the security group.
[07:35] Raj Patel: Good. One operational nuance: what if third-party dependent region has throttling? The runbook should have a region-fallback.
[07:42] Lena Park: We can add a fallback policy: route traffic to a secondary region or fall back to a smaller model variant in the same region — both options are supported. The decision tree will include latency and cost thresholds to pick which fallback to use.
[07:56] Daniel Cho: Any updates on SLA for Dedicated burst during canary? We need a firm guarantee.
[08:00] Maya Chen: For POC we'll provide best-effort reserved capacity; if enterprise contract is signed we can lock a short-term SLA. For the canary weekend, we can provision a dedicated pool with higher priority and notify support.
[08:12] Sofia Martinez: One last sync: who is the exec escalation if the canary goes sideways?
[08:17] Maya Chen: We'll include an escalation matrix in the runbook: on-call SE, CSM (Lena), AE escalation (Maya), then Ops lead (Raj), then CTO contact.
[08:28] Raj Patel: Sounds good. We'll need the runbook in doc form with step-by-step commands.
[08:33] Maya Chen: We'll deliver that by Thursday EOD (2027-05-05).
[08:37] Omar Singh: And I'll push the warmup script + health shim and recommended autoscale settings also by Thursday.
[08:42] Priya Nair: I'll confirm the security artifact locations by Friday the 7th.
[08:47] Alex Kim: I'll get finance to review the cost table once Maya sends it.
[08:50] Maya Chen: Perfect. Any other topics?
[08:53] [pause]
[08:58] Daniel Cho: Quick question — competitors. Someone asked if we considered Replicloud — how do you compare?
[09:05] Omar Singh: Replicloud is similar on raw throughput but lacks the unified rollout tooling and the traffic gating we provide out-of-the-box; AtlasAI has strong model cataloging but less mature on private VPC options. We'll send a short comparison note.
[09:20] Maya Chen: OK, wrapping — recap of next steps: runbook, warmup script, schedule canary, confirm KMS/SSO artifacts, and finance review. We'll reconvene after the canary data is in next week.
[09:34] Raj Patel: Thanks all.
[09:36] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — meeting adjourned.

[Post-call notes]:
- Shared links: runbook draft (will be updated), warmup script repo link (pending Omar), dashboard links (read-only until canary), gated metric spreadsheet.
- Risk areas: autoscaler oscillation, KV cache warmup time, cost delta for pre-warm.
- Recommended small pilot: Saturday 2027-05-08 01:00–07:00 (tentative)
